title: Make sense of a spreadsheet on the shop-sales sample
objective: Prove that a small local model can run the Make sense of a spreadsheet craftbook on its bundled shop-sales sample, offline, and reach the terminal step with a findings report whose numbers come from the file.
prompt: What stands out in this spreadsheet of a small bakery's monthly sales?

setup.about: A small made-up bakery's 2025 sales: one row per product per month, with units sold and revenue in euros. No web access or outside data is needed.
setup.missionObjectives: Run the craftbook on source/sales.csv and leave findings.md in the task folder, with every number taken from the file.

worker.name: Data Analyst
worker.about: A careful data analyst. Follow the craftbook steps exactly, read the file you are given, and never invent a number.

success.summary: The spreadsheet-findings task read the sample, wrote findings.md with all four sections and a table, named the December peak and the falling rye loaf, and reached its terminal step without external services.

axes.name: grounding
axes.description: Every number, product and month in findings.md appears in sales.csv or is a correct sum of values in it.

axes.name: insight
axes.description: The findings name what a shop owner would want to know first: the December peak driven by the honey spice cake, and the steady fall of the rye loaf.

rubric.contextNote: Advisory only. Deterministic pass/fail comes from the craftbook runtime gates, the deliverable checks, attribution, and terminal progress.

qualityFocus: numbers quoted from the file, never invented
all four required sections and a derived table
